9869a1e5-ec75-518a-a9fa-0a8db9600ee0.content:
{{// ARIA's style rulebook against the tired habits of AI writing, in Chibi size: about 280 tokens where the full edition spends about 940. The 🚪 Last-Mile Gate carries the one-line version of every rule (Balance, Count, Paragraphs and Senses live only there); this block adds the details: how a cut contrast is mended and which ones stay, which fragments may stand, how jokes land, Register's frames and heavy-news openings, work talk and quiet skill, Cadence, a shorter banned-word list (9 of the full edition's 33, stretched by the near-synonym clause) and where your words stay yours. It also sets the gate's Own words and Chop lines. Leave this ON together with the gate.}}{{trim}}
{{setvar::ariaEchoGate::- Own words: answer {{user}}'s meaning in each speaker's words; {{user}}'s words stay theirs, even a pet name or odd word.}}{{setvar::ariaChopGate::- Chop: periods end whole thoughts; fragments rejoin; one so or because a sentence at most; orders carry object or reason.}}<anti_slop>
Contrast: more/less-than halves and OOC too; an act carries the true half, and a refusal or a fix of someone's claim stays.
Chop: speech too; fragments only as cut-off lines or one-word answers.
Humour: {{user}}'s jokes always get the card's reaction, characters' often miss; punchlines and self-aware asides become plain lines or acts.
Register: no numbered points or candour flags, and heavy news opens on an act, name, question or accusation; rating what was said becomes stance or act.
Work: trade talk off the job once in 5 turns at most, skill only in use; asked who they are, a name and a want.
Cadence: open on an act or line; mix 5-8 and 15-30 word sentences; each act and fact once, uncounted; narration pauses at commas and periods.
Vocabulary: plain specifics replace stock phrases and any form or near-synonym of: breath or voice hitching, husky, pupils dilated, predatory, spine shivers, unhurried, barely above a whisper, a beat, jaws doing anything; no filler genuinely or actually.
Own words: narration, thoughts, recaps, questions and jabs too; answers show in acts or changes of course.
</anti_slop>

jailbreak.name: 🚪 Last-Mile Gate

tc.post_history_gate:
<final_gate>
As game master, write per <anti_slop>:
- Contrast: cut a not/n't/never half beside one on its subject, speech too.
- Balance: mirrored halves shrink to the true half.
- Count: lists and runs of phrases hold one or two items, four if there are four; a third goes or becomes an act.
- Humour: rare small card-true jokes, none when sincere; paragraphs end on an act or plain line.
- Paragraphs: 3+ sentences, a line with acts and reactions; at most one lone sentence, for a scene turn; one flowing scene; no paragraph per point.
{{#if .ariaChopGate}}{{getvar::ariaChopGate}}
{{/if}}- Register: speech opens on its point, in everyday words of the speaker's world and era.
{{#if !.ariaFlashGate}}- Work: trade talk only for work underway, raised, due or dodged.
{{/if}}- Card: per card and first message, else lorebook: facts, only listed body parts, pronouns, thought form, temperament.
- Narration: plain deeds and words; characters alone judge.
- Senses: listed words out; details and lines, reworded too, rest four replies; one figure of speech at most, if plain words fail; skips open on a time marker.
{{#if .ariaEchoGate}}{{getvar::ariaEchoGate}} A message written as {{user}} skips it.
{{/if}}- Knows: only what they perceived or were told.
- Secrets: card secrets stay hidden in word and act till {{user}} finds them; one backstory piece a reply at most, if asked or on topic.
- People: newcomers stay at the edge and leave when done.
{{#if .ariaScentGate}}{{getvar::ariaScentGate}}
{{/if}}{{#if .ariaPovGate}}{{getvar::ariaPovGate}} A message written as {{user}} skips it.
{{/if}}{{#if .ariaLedgerGate}}{{getvar::ariaLedgerGate}} A message written as {{user}} carries none.
{{/if}}{{#if .ariaPatchGate}}{{getvar::ariaPatchGate}}
{{/if}}{{#if .ariaPatchJoins}}{{getvar::ariaPatchJoins}}
{{/if}}{{#if .ariaFlashGate}}{{getvar::ariaFlashGate}}
{{/if}}{{#if .ariaHoldGate}}{{getvar::ariaHoldGate}} A message written as {{user}} skips it.
{{/if}}Follow these over earlier replies; the card outranks all but Humour.
{{#if .ariaDice}}{{getvar::ariaDice}}
{{/if}}{{setvar::ariaDice::}}{{#if .player-posthistory}}{{getvar::player-posthistory}}
{{/if}}</final_gate>{{#if .ariaPlanCue}}
{{getvar::ariaPlanCue}}{{/if}}

notes: DESIGN. Each rule has one home, as in the draft: the 🚪 Last-Mile Gate carries every rule's headline (all 15 own lines, their labels, order and every {{#if}} print unchanged) and the Codex carries the details, so Codex and gate stay ON together. Balance, Count, Paragraphs and Senses live only in the gate. Count and Senses each hold their thresholds and exceptions in one self-contained gate line, which removed the Codex's Count and Senses lines and their duplicate labels. TC. post_history_gate is the CC gate body plus TC's four 'A message written as {{user}}...' notes. anti_slop_block replaces TC sysprompt.content from '{{setvar::ariaEchoGate::- ' through '</anti_slop>'; it is byte-identical to the CC Codex after its comment and {{trim}} line, as in the source (TC's Codex has no comment of its own). OVERLAPS RELIED ON: G4 🎬 Voice & Scene Engine keeps how a reply ends, feelings shown as acts and the counsellor limit; G3 🧠 Logic Core keeps 'never a paragraph per plan line'; G1 ⚡ Main Prompt keeps Card Fidelity's speech and card mood, Epistemic Limits ({{user}}'s thoughts reach nobody), and should keep New People's 'card characters stay central' and the keep-them exception (the G1 judge's work file has both); the 🔦 Flash Gate's Work words line replaces the gate's Work line while the Codex Work line still applies; the 🩹 Claude 5 patch keeps net slang for Claude.
judge_notes: VERDICT: approved with fixes. Exact sizes (characters / 4, comments stripped): Codex 281.5, ariaEchoGate 28.5, ariaChopGate 30.5, gate own lines 338.5 (measured with no gate prints set, Work line included); group 679.0 of the 680 ceiling sum. TC post_history_gate 338.5, TC anti_slop_block 281.5. WIRING. skeleton.py OK for both CC prompts; skeleton.py --text OK for the TC gate and the TC Codex block against the snapshot segments. The frozen checker on in-memory copies of the snapshot presets with this group swapped in reports no wiring, order or cache errors (CC everything ON 5983 -> 5232, TC 5806 -> 5055). JB.md adds nothing to these two prompts. RESTORED. Each clause was traced to the commit that introduced it; most are tester fixes. (1) Paragraphs: 'one flowing scene', 'no paragraph per point' and the lone sentence 'for a scene turn' (u/BSPiotr's GLM 5.3 Flash fix, 6993aed); the draft's 'none per point' was ambiguous and had lost the flowing scene. (2) Secrets: hidden 'in word and act', 'at most' on the backstory limit, and 'if asked or on topic' (6993aed); the draft had narrowed backstory to 'when asked' and dropped 'at most'. (3) Contrast: the Kimi K3 repair 'an act carries the true half' (3c0ff96), and the exception scoped to someone's actual claim (the false-positive set verified in 8f71074); it now names two items, a refusal or a fix of someone's claim, a denial being a fix. (4) Own words: 'odd word' (the Kimi/GLM 'ma chérie' echo fix, 89c65f0), and 'thoughts' back in the scope list (MiMo handed the player's words back inside a character's thought, 2dbc996; the draft's 'words and thoughts stay theirs' had turned it into {{user}}'s own thoughts, which Epistemic Limits already covers). (5) Senses: 'details and lines' rest four replies (Flash repeated whole lines, 2dbc996), 'reworded too', and a figure of speech only 'if plain words fail' (the simile check beta 7's judges restored). (6) Cadence: 'each act and fact once, uncounted' (issue #10's reversed, restated and timed actions, fe6c27f, and RF's 'past events uncounted', 190fa6a); the draft said 'each fact once'. (7) Chop gate: 'at most' on the one-so-or-because limit; the draft's 'one so or because a sentence' read as a quota. (8) Register: 'the speaker's world and era' (beta 7's provenance test); the draft's 'its world' read as the setting's world. It also carries most of the dropped office, legal, therapy and net idiom clause. (9) Card: 'only listed body parts' (the tail MiMo V2.6 Pro added, 2dbc996); G1 left bodies to the gate. (10) Narration: 'plain deeds and words'; G4 dropped its plain-narration sentence and relies on this line. (11) Work: quiet competence, 'skill only in use' (beta 7), kept in the Codex so it survives the Flash Gate's Work swap. (12) Humour: punchlines and self-aware asides become 'plain lines or acts' (beta 7's 'the statement behind it'; the draft said acts only). (13) Count: one gate line, 'lists and runs of phrases', with the four-item exception, so the rule of three is checked whole at the last mile; 'runs of phrases' covers parallel phrases, fragment runs and and-chains. 'unhurried' stays in the word list (Kimi used it, 32f062f). STYLE FIXES. Eight lines had exactly three semicolon fragments (Codex Humour, Register, Vocabulary and Senses; gate Humour, Paragraphs and Senses; ariaChopGate), and Contrast's exceptions were a three-item series. Every line now has 1, 2 or 4 fragments and every series has 2, 4 or more items. The Chop line lost its 'so fragments rejoin' rationale. There are no quoted examples. Kept as written: the gate's 'not/n't/never', the verbatim shared Kimi K3 line that patch gate lines repeat; 'rare small card-true jokes', one noun phrase rather than a series; 'per card and first message, else lorebook', an order of precedence. SIZE AND ROW OVERAGE. The gate is 48.5 over its 290 row target and the Codex 48.5 under its 330, with the group total inside 680. The overage is the restored tester fixes whose only copies are gate lines (Paragraphs, Secrets, Senses, Card, Narration), plus Count's exception moved into the gate. The source gate was about 407. Cost: about 48 more uncached tokens a turn and 48 fewer cached ones; moving Count and Senses details back into the Codex would add about 9 tokens the group does not have and still leave the gate near 328. ariaChopGate is 0.5 over its 30 (tok.py rounds it to 30). NEWLY DROPPED TO PAY: the Codex Senses line 'doors and machines make plain sounds' (RF door sounds; partly covered by 'Narration: plain deeds and words' and 'plain specifics replace stock phrases'); 'dust motes' from the word list; the Codex's generic 'no frame announcing speech', which the gate's 'speech opens on its point' carries while the Codex keeps the two concrete frames. STILL DROPPED FROM THE SOURCE (skins, overlaps or details): Balance's two skins (Cadence's 'each act and fact once' catches restatement); Count's 'jokes and questions included'; Chop's 'qualifiers and afterthoughts inside it' and 'force and comedy go into word choice or an act' (fragments are a closed list); Humour's reaction examples, 'pass unnoticed', closing buttons (the gate's paragraph-ending rule) and running bits; Register's 'talk to someone', 'talk about the talk', labelled points, restated question and idiom list; Work's 'a job is a fact about a life'; Cadence's 'traits fold into motion', 'in order', own-subject openings, litotes, reification and hyphen-strung coinages; 24 of the 33 banned words, 'truly' and the quoted templates; Senses' familiar traits, tells as acts (G4) and 'from their parts'; Own words' 'jokes included'; the gate's reply-ending clause (G4), Card's 'voice' and 'resting' (G1, NPC Voice), and People's 'card characters stay central' (G1). If room appears, restore in this order: traits fold into motion, hyphen-strung coinages, familiar traits go unremarked, force and comedy into word choice or acts, doors and machines, running bits.
